    PKG[("data packages")] --> BE
    HUB["hub (future)"] -.-> PKG

docs.title: core
docs.text:
Responsibility. The domain model and the modelling methods, as a pure Python library: entities indexed by spatial unit × social group × service × time, uncertain values, the variable catalogue, scenario overlays, the model registry and, later, the methods of the four papers. No web framework, no database driver, no file-system side effects in model code (AGENTS.md, core rules).

Main entry points and folders (core/src/solidaritynode_core/):

Module Papers State in 0.1.0 model all implemented: entities, identifiers, IndexedValues, uncertain values, ordinal states, service-unit quantities, variable catalogue, tickets, trajectories, study area, message catalogue, model registry (get_registry) scenarios 1 §13, 3 §7–10 implemented (platform part): scenario overlay apply_overlay, placeholders, order of application (OQ-30, proposed) uncertainty 1 §11, 2 §14, 3 §22 partly: summary statistics of samples (mean, median, interval quantiles); Monte Carlo propagation not yet validation 1 §14, 2 §18, 3 §24 partly: the diagnostic model diagnostic-v0 (validation/diagnostic.py), not a method; validation tools not yet bayes 1–4 interfaces only (engine: ADR 0004, proposed) accessibility, demand, capacity, service_gap 1 typed interfaces only, no method latent_need 2 typed interfaces only, no method vulnerability 3 typed interfaces only, no method operations, dynamics, resilience 4 typed interfaces only, no method sensitivity 1 §12, 2 §16, 3 §23 empty interface

The module map and what each module will compute: domain model §6.

Configuration. None: core reads no environment variables. Randomness only through an explicit seed or numpy.random.Generator.

Tests. core/tests/ with pytest (make test-core); make lint-core runs ruff and mypy in strict mode. test_package.py enforces the dependency direction (no web or database imports); test_demo_dataset.py and test_diagnostic.py check known answers on the synthetic demo data.

Related. ADR 0003, 0004, 0005, 0016; Spec 00 §2–6.

docs.title: backend
docs.text:
Responsibility. The HTTP API and persistence: sign-in and roles, data package validation and import, study area, scenarios and their versions, runs (creating jobs, never computing in a request), results, comparison and export. The same code runs as a municipal installation or a hub (DEPLOYMENT_MODE, ADR 0012); only the municipal role is complete.

Main entry points and folders (backend/src/solidaritynode_backend/):

Path What main.py FastAPI application; mounts only the routes of the deployment role routers/ auth, users, data (study area, packages), scenarios, runs, health (/health, /health/ready, /version); requests (tickets, municipality only, stores nothing yet) and hub (hub only, placeholder) services/ packages, study area, runs, samples, export, throttling, installation role schemas/ Pydantic models of the API, the scenario schema (docs/schemas/scenario.schema.json) and tickets orm.py, db.py, ../../migrations/ SQLAlchemy models; Alembic migrations (the only way the schema changes) jobs/ JobRunner protocol and PostgresJobRunner (ADR 0006) cli.py import-package, activate-version, create-admin, seed-demo-users, wait-runs, export-schemas, check-config, clear-login-locks (called by make targets) messages.py server message catalogue with stable codes (translated by the frontend)

Configuration. APP_ENV, DEPLOYMENT_MODE, POSTGRES_* or SOLIDARITYNODE_DATABASE_URL, SOLIDARITYNODE_CORS_ORIGINS, SOLIDARITYNODE_LOG_LEVEL, SOLIDARITYNODE_SESSION_*, SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_*, SOLIDARITYNODE_TRUSTED_PROXIES, SOLIDARITYNODE_BASEMAP, SOLIDARITYNODE_RESULTS_DIR, SOLIDARITYNODE_PACKAGES_DIR, SOLIDARITYNODE_RESULT_INTERVAL_QUANTILES, SOLIDARITYNODE_SAMPLES_WARN_MB, GIT_COMMIT. make check-config APP_ENV=production validates them.

Tests. backend/tests/ with pytest against a throw-away PostGIS database (make test-db, then make test-backend): authentication and roles, packages and the update flow, scenarios, runs, provenance, samples, the worker, settings, messages, the ticket schema.

Related. ADR 0006, 0008, 0012, 0013, 0015, 0016, 0017; backend rules.

docs.title: worker
docs.text:
Responsibility. Claims queued jobs from PostgreSQL (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), runs the model from the core registry, reports progress, honours cancel requests, writes result summaries to the database and samples to the results volume. A running job holds a lease (jobs.heartbeat_at); any worker fails a job whose lease expired.

Entry point. python -m solidaritynode_backend.worker (worker.py), the worker service in compose.yaml, same image as the backend.

Configuration. SOLIDARITYNODE_WORKER_NAME, SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS, SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_STALE_SECONDS, SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS, SOLIDARITYNODE_DIAGNOSTIC_STEP_DELAY_S, plus the database, results and GIT_COMMIT settings of the backend.

Tests. backend/tests/test_worker.py, test_runs.py, test_run_provenance.py; UAT steps on cancel and a stopped worker (UAT 01, sections G and I).

Related. ADR 0006, 0017. Lifecycle: run lifecycle.

docs.title: frontend
docs.text:
Responsibility. Displays; never computes. Screens: login, study area, scenarios, scenario editor, run, compare, admin, health (user guide). Maps with Leaflet; uncertainty always shown; English and Greek.

Main entry points and folders (frontend/src/): main.tsx, App.tsx (routes), pages/ (one component per screen), map/ (map view, patterns, colour scales), api/ (client.ts and schema.d.ts generated from docs/schemas/openapi.json by make schemas), i18n/ (en.json, el.json, server message translations), app/ (session). In the container, nginx (frontend/nginx/default.conf.template) serves the build and proxies /api/* to the backend.

Configuration. Build argument GIT_COMMIT (shown in the footer); the basemap comes from the backend (SOLIDARITYNODE_BASEMAP). Ports: FRONTEND_HOST_PORT.

Tests. Vitest and Testing Library next to the components (*.test.tsx, make test-frontend); a test fails when a server message code has no translation. Playwright end-to-end tests in frontend/e2e/ (make test-e2e, CI job e2e). make lint-frontend: ESLint, Prettier, tsc.

Related. ADR 0007; frontend rules; glossary.

docs.title: db
docs.text:
Responsibility. PostgreSQL with PostGIS (docker.io/postgis/postgis), in the named volume db-data. Holds users and sessions, sign-in throttling, the installation role, data versions with their features, records, coverage and warnings, scenarios and versions, jobs, runs, result summaries and tables. Data model: Lifecycles and data model.

Configuration. POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DB_HOST_PORT. The backend container runs alembic upgrade head on start.

Tests. Every backend test runs against a throw-away database on a real PostGIS server. make db-shell opens psql (UAT guide).

Related. ADR 0008, 0013.

docs.title: Results storage
docs.text:
Responsibility. Full Monte Carlo samples of every run in Parquet (runs/<run id>/samples.parquet, sorted, zstd, with run metadata and a SHA-256 checked on read and export), and uploaded package archives. The database keeps only summaries (mean, median, interval quantiles) for maps and tables. Nothing is deleted automatically; the Admin screen shows disk usage.

Configuration. SOLIDARITYNODE_RESULTS_DIR (/data/results, the results volume, in compose), SOLIDARITYNODE_SAMPLES_WARN_MB.

Tests. backend/tests/test_samples.py, test_run_provenance.py.

Related. ADR 0008, 0017. Backups: the database and the results volume must be backed up together; a backup guide is not written yet.

docs.title: Data packages
docs.text:
Responsibility. The only way data enters an installation: a versioned, checksummed bundle for one study area plus a buffer, with manifest.json (files, checksums, layer coverage and licences, changelog, DP-NNN processing notes), layers.gpkg (GeoPackage in the projected CRS of the manifest), tables/ (strict CSV) and checks/ (hand-checked values). Imported after validation and a preview of changes, in one transaction; every version is kept.

Where. Demo packages 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 in data/synthetic/packages/ (built by scripts/build_demo_packages.py, DP-002); import code in backend/.../services/packages.py; make import-package, make activate-version.

Configuration. SOLIDARITYNODE_PACKAGES_DIR (packages offered on the Admin screen).

Tests. backend/tests/test_packages.py, test_update_flow.py; UAT 01 sections J and K.

Related. ADR 0013; OQ-28 (buffer); Data packages and updates.

docs.title: Hub (future)
docs.text:
Responsibility. Keeps national raw sources, onboards municipalities step by step (clip with buffer, clean, check, DP-NNN notes), keeps a coverage matrix per municipality and publishes data packages. When a municipality is onboarded or corrected, it publishes new packages for every study area whose buffer includes it. Optionally receives aggregated, anonymised indicators from municipalities (ADR 0014, open).

State in 0.1.0. DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hub exists and mounts only placeholder hub routes (routers/hub.py); onboarding is the next step on the roadmap (milestone v0.2 Hub onboarding).

Related. ADR 0009, 0012, 0013, 0014; Spec 00 §3 (Onboarding, Deployment).

docs.text: Describes platform version 0.1.0. Diagrams are Mermaid and change in the same pull request as the behaviour they describe (AGENTS.md). Components: Components.

docs.title: Run lifecycle
docs.text:
A run is created by the backend and executed by the worker; the request handler never computes (ADR 0006, 0017).

sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Analyst
    participant FE as frontend
    participant API as backend
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant W as worker
    participant C as core (model registry)
    participant R as results volume

    U->>FE: Run this version (seed optional)
    FE->>API: POST /runs {scenario, version, seed, config}
    API->>API: draw a seed if none, input hash of scenario version,<br/>data version, code, model, seed, configuration
    alt a succeeded run has the same hash and its samples file passes SHA-256
        API-->>FE: existing run (reused, nothing computed)
    else no reusable run
        API->>DB: insert run + job (status queued), samples size estimate
        API-->>FE: new run (queued)
        W->>DB: claim job (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), status running
        W->>C: model(study area, scenario overlay, config, seed, progress)
        loop every progress step
            C-->>W: progress
            W->>DB: progress, heartbeat, read cancel flag
        end
        W->>R: samples.parquet (+ SHA-256)
        W->>DB: result summaries (mean, median, interval), tables,<br/>environment, job succeeded
    end
    loop until finished
        FE->>API: GET /runs/{id}
        API-->>FE: status, progress, results when succeeded
    end

docs.title: Run statuses
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued: POST /runs (no reusable run)
    queued --> running: a worker claims the job
    queued --> cancelled: Cancel run
    running --> succeeded: results stored
    running --> failed: error, worker stopped, lease expired,<br/>maximum runtime, queued under other code
    running --> cancelled: Cancel run (at the next progress step)
    succeeded --> [*]
    failed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

Finished runs never change. Only a succeeded run is reused; after failed or cancelled, starting again creates a new run.

docs.title: Data update flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Administrator
    participant API as backend
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant W as worker

    A->>API: preview package (server directory or uploaded archive)
    API->>API: verify checksums, validate schema 2.0,<br/>compare with the active version
    API-->>A: status (new, update, already imported), changes per layer,<br/>coverage changes, changelog, problems
    A->>API: confirm import
    API->>DB: one transaction: new data version with features, records,<br/>coverage and warnings, it becomes active, earlier ones are kept
    API->>DB: queue a baseline run on the new version
    API->>DB: revalidate every scenario against the new version
    API-->>A: imported, scenarios that need attention
    W->>DB: run the baseline (run lifecycle above)
    Note over A,API: Rollback: "Make 1.0.0 active again" (or make activate-version)<br/>does the same three steps for an earlier version, nothing is deleted

docs.title: Data version states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> previewed: preview (nothing stored)
    previewed --> [*]: cancel, or refused (checksum or validation)
    previewed --> active: confirm import
    active --> kept: another version is imported or activated
    kept --> active: make it active again (rollback)

Runs always point to the data version they used, whatever its state.

The persistent model in PostgreSQL (backend/src/solidaritynode_backend/orm.py and backend/migrations/). Feature-level tables of a data version (data_features, data_records, data_coverage, data_warnings), sessions, sign-in throttling and the installation role are left out for clarity.

        text unit_id
        text group_id
        text service_id
        text time_label
        float mean
        float median
        float low
        float high
        bool edge_effect_warning
    }
    SAMPLES_FILE {
        text path
        text sha256

A result belongs to exactly one run. A run stores the scenario version it used, so later versions of the scenario never change it. Full Monte Carlo samples live in the Parquet file; the database keeps the summaries used by maps and tables (ADR 0008, 0017).

docs.title: Ticket workflow
docs.text:
The rules are in AGENTS.md and the contributing guide; this page shows how a ticket moves. Live state: the Kintsugi board.

flowchart TB
    I["Issue<br/>acceptance criteria, spec section, OQ-n"] --> Q{"Spec clear and<br/>OQs decided?"}
    Q -- no --> RQ["Comment the question on the issue<br/>label needs-spec; stop"]
    RQ --> DEC["Decision in open-questions.md or an ADR<br/>(paper-revisions.md if the method changes)"]
    DEC --> Q
    Q -- yes --> B["Branch feat/ISSUE-short-name"]

docs.text: After merges accumulate, the maintainer cuts a release: Releasing.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Human-readable versions of the area rules. The rules themselves live in AGENTS.md files, which every coding agent and every contributor reads:

Area Rules (short, for agents) Explanations (for humans) Whole repository AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md core/ core/AGENTS.md core.md backend/ backend/AGENTS.md backend.md frontend/ frontend/AGENTS.md frontend.md data-processing/ data-processing/AGENTS.md data-processing.md

The root AGENTS.md always applies; an area file adds rules for its folder. If the two conflict, the root wins and the conflict is reported as an issue.

CLAUDE.md files are only bridges for Claude Code (they import the AGENTS.md next to them) and never contain rules.

To propose a rule change, see "Maintaining these instructions" in the root AGENTS.md and "Changing the rules" in CONTRIBUTING.md. Every rule here has the same wording as in its AGENTS.md, plus a one-line reason and, where useful, an example.

docs.title: Backend conventions
docs.text: Rules: backend/AGENTS.md. The root AGENTS.md also applies.

docs.title: Request handlers create jobs
docs.text:
Request handlers never run long computations; they create jobs (ADR 0006).

Why: simulations can take minutes; a blocked handler times out and holds a worker.

Example (illustrative; the runs endpoints do not exist yet): POST /runs validates the scenario, enqueues the run and returns 202 with the run id; the client polls the run status.

docs.title: Runs are immutable and reproducible
docs.text:
Record every reproducibility field: scenario version, data version, code commit, model id and version, seed, configuration (Spec 00 §3, ADR 0017).

Why: a result is only useful as evidence if the same inputs reproduce it.

docs.title: Database changes through Alembic only
docs.text:
Change the schema only through Alembic migrations, and never edit a migration that has been merged; add a new one instead.

Why: installations that already applied a merged migration would silently diverge.

docs.title: Authorisation on every endpoint
docs.text:
Check authorisation on every endpoint that reads or writes scenarios, runs, results, users or data packages.

Why: scenarios have owners and visibility, and installations hold municipal data (ADR 0015 decides the mechanism).

docs.title: Privacy of tickets and operational data
docs.text:
Tickets and other operational data follow the privacy rules (OQ-21, ADR 0010). Never log request bodies that could contain them.

Why: logs are copied, shipped and kept longer than the database; a logged body defeats anonymity by design.

docs.title: Settings from the environment
docs.text:
Settings come from environment variables documented in .env.example (see "Configuration" in CONTRIBUTING.md).

Why: development must run with no manual editing of .env, and production values are never committed.

docs.title: Core conventions
docs.text: Rules: core/AGENTS.md. The root AGENTS.md also applies.

docs.title: Implement only what a spec states
docs.text:
Every public function cites its spec section, and OQ-n where relevant.

Why: the papers and docs/specs/ are the source of truth; open questions are decided by the maintainers, not in code.

Example: a docstring line such as Spec 00 §4; OQ-8. Where an open question blocks the behaviour, raise NotImplementedError and cite it.

docs.title: No web frameworks, database drivers or file-system side effects in model code
docs.text:
I/O lives at the edges (loaders and writers), not in model functions.

Why: core must stay a pure, testable library usable from the backend, notebooks and tests. Imports of web frameworks and drivers are already blocked by tests/test_package.py and the ruff banned-api rule; file-system side effects are checked in review.

docs.title: Explicit randomness
docs.text:
Randomness only through an explicit numpy.random.Generator or seed argument.

Why: runs must be reproducible from their recorded seed (ADR 0017).

Example: def sample(..., rng: numpy.random.Generator), never numpy.random.random().

docs.title: Units and reference periods
docs.text:
Quantities carry their service unit and reference period. Never add quantities of different services or periods.

Why: a visit, a bed-day and a home-care hour are not comparable (OQ-24); summing them gives a meaningless number.

docs.title: Known-answer tests
docs.text:
Every algorithm has a known-answer test on the synthetic demo data (data/synthetic/demo/, DP-001).

Why: a hand-checked expected value catches errors that property tests and type checks miss.

docs.title: Model ids and versions
docs.text:
Bump model ids and versions whenever outputs can change.

Why: runs record the model version (ADR 0017); an unchanged version with different outputs breaks reproducibility.

docs.title: Data-processing conventions
docs.text: Rules: data-processing/AGENTS.md. The root AGENTS.md also applies.

docs.title: A processing note for every processed dataset
docs.text:
Every processed dataset has a DP-NNN note copied from docs/data-processing/TEMPLATE.md.

Why: a dataset is only as trustworthy as the record of how it was made.

Example: DP-001, the synthetic demo dataset.

docs.title: Relative paths, no data files
docs.text:
QGIS projects use relative paths. Commit no data files; only models, scripts, styles and projects.

Why: absolute paths break on every other machine, and data may be real or licensed (see "Data and privacy rules" in the root AGENTS.md).

docs.title: Exact QGIS calls in the note
docs.text:
Copy the exact QGIS calls from Processing → History into the note.

Why: the history holds the exact algorithm ids and parameters; a prose description cannot be re-run.

docs.title: QGIS is a preparation tool only
docs.text:
QGIS is never a runtime dependency of core or backend.

Why: the platform must install and run without a desktop GIS.

docs.title: Frontend conventions
docs.text: Rules: frontend/AGENTS.md. The root AGENTS.md also applies.

docs.title: No scientific or modelling logic in the frontend
docs.text:
All computation happens in core and reaches the UI through the backend API; the frontend only displays.

Why: one implementation of each method, tested in one place, and every displayed number traceable to a run.

Example: to show a coverage ratio, read it from the result endpoint; do not divide capacity by demand in a component.

docs.title: One API client
docs.text:
Generate the client from the backend OpenAPI schema or type it to match the schema. No hand-written duplicate types.

Why: duplicate types drift silently from the backend.

docs.title: Always show uncertainty
docs.text:
Show an interval, distribution or probability, never a bare number.

Why: domain invariant 6 (outputs carry uncertainty); a bare point estimate reads as certain.

Example: "0.42 (90 % interval 0.31–0.55)" rather than "0.42".

docs.title: Mark lower-confidence results
docs.text:
Visibly mark results from the diagnostic model, units with an edge-effect warning (study-area buffer, OQ-28), and features whose quality is estimated or open_data (Spec 00 §3, stable identifiers and history).

Why: users must see when a result rests on weaker data or a weaker model before acting on it.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Label every control, support keyboard navigation, use colour scales readable by colour-blind users, and give text alternatives for map information where practical.

Why: municipal staff and the public must be able to use the platform; maps alone exclude some users.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
All user-facing text goes through translation files (Greek and English). No hard-coded strings in components.

Why: the platform is used in Greek and English; strings scattered in components are missed in translation.

docs.title: Greek terms follow the glossary; server texts are translated by code
docs.text:
Use the terms of docs/i18n/glossary.md (for example τρωτότητα for vulnerability, φαινόμενο ορίου for edge effect, ανοιχτά δεδομένα for open data). Add a missing term to the glossary in the same pull request. Texts that come from the server (errors, reference problems, "recorded only" lines, run failures) are shown with serverText(t, text), which matches them against the exported templates (src/api/messages.json) and shows server.<code>.

Why: one concept translated two ways confuses users and reviewers; server texts in English inside the Greek UI were the most visible gap in UAT.

docs.title: Libraries only as decided in ADRs
docs.text:
Use the map library and other major libraries only as decided in ADRs (for example ADR 0007, map library).

Why: major libraries shape the architecture and must pass the licence check.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Component tests with Vitest and Testing Library; main user flows with Playwright.

Why: component tests catch display regressions quickly; end-to-end tests cover what the maintainer checks in UAT.

docs.title: Data processing notes
docs.text: Every dataset that ends up in a data package, a study area or a paper has a processing note here. The note says where the data came from, what was done to it (in QGIS or elsewhere), and how to check the result. It is the source for the "Data" sections of the papers and for the provenance listed in each data package manifest.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
docs/data-processing/
├── README.md                 this file
├── TEMPLATE.md               copy this for a new note
└── DP-001-osm-road-network.md, DP-002-elstat-population.md, ...

data-processing/              (repo root) reproducible processing files
├── qgis/
│   ├── models/               QGIS Processing models (.model3)
│   ├── scripts/              PyQGIS / Processing scripts (.py)
│   └── projects/             QGIS project files (.qgz), relative paths only
└── styles/                   layer styles (.qml) used in QGIS and for checking

data/local/                   real input and output data (git-ignored, never committed)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. One note per processed dataset, named DP-NNN-short-name.md, numbered in order. Never renumber.
  2. Record every step, including manual edits. For QGIS tools, copy the exact call from Processing → History (it shows the algorithm id and all parameters as Python) into the note.
  3. Make it repeatable. If a sequence of steps will be run again (for example for another municipality or a data update), turn it into a Processing model (.model3, built with the Graphical Modeler) or a script in data-processing/qgis/, and link it from the note. Manual edits that cannot be automated (for example fixing a misplaced facility) are listed one by one with the reason.
  4. QGIS projects use relative paths (Project → Properties → General → Save paths: Relative) and point to data/local/. No absolute paths such as C:\Users\....
  5. No real data in git. Inputs and outputs live in data/local/. Only notes, models, scripts, styles and projects are committed. Operational or personal data are never processed here.
  6. Record versions: QGIS version (Help → About), plugin versions, and the date and version of each source dataset.
  7. Checks are part of the note: what was compared, counts before and after, CRS, a screenshot of the result if useful (store it next to the note, small PNG).
  8. Licences: each source is also listed in docs/data-sources.md. If processing creates a derived database (for example from OpenStreetMap, ODbL), note the attribution and share-alike obligations.
  9. Link to packages: the manifest.json of each data package lists the DP-NNN notes of the data it contains.
  10. If a processing step changes something the method depends on (for example how population is assigned to units), add an entry to docs/specs/paper-revisions.md or an open question.

docs.title: How a paper becomes a spec
docs.text:
1. The original text is stored unchanged in docs/specs/source/ (see its README).
  2. A per-paper spec docs/specs/NN-name.md restates the paper section by section in implementable form: definitions, inputs and outputs with units and dimensions, formulas as decided, and the paper section each item comes from (for example Paper 1 §7). It uses the OQ-1 notation.
  3. Every per-paper spec ends with an "Open questions" section listing the OQ-n that affect it and what remains undefined.
  4. When a decision is taken: update open-questions.md (status and reasoning), paper-revisions.md (text changes), 00-domain-model.md (model), the per-paper spec, and, if behaviour changes, the code and its docstrings.

docs.title: How code refers to the spec
docs.text:
• Every public type and function in core cites its source (for example Paper 3 §15, or Spec 00 §4.4 where no paper section exists) in its docstring.
  • Where code touches an open question, the docstring names it (OQ-n) and the behaviour stays undefined (an abstract interface or NotImplementedError).
  • The variable catalogue in core/src/solidaritynode_core/model/catalogue.py mirrors Spec 00 §4; tests check that BN nodes, computed variables and scenario parameters stay distinct.
  • Technical decisions go to ADRs in docs/adr/.

docs.title: Domain model (v0 draft)
docs.text: Status: DRAFT for human review. This is a digest of Papers 1–4. The original texts will be stored verbatim in docs/specs/source/ and as per-paper specs 01–04. Where this digest and a paper disagree, the paper wins and this file must be corrected. Anything the papers leave unspecified is listed in open-questions.md as OQ-n and must not be resolved in code or in this file.

docs.title: 1. Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    P1["Paper 1<br/>Accessibility, capacity,<br/>demand, service gap"] --> P2["Paper 2<br/>Social susceptibility,<br/>hidden need, total need"]
    P1 --> P3
    P2 --> P3["Paper 3<br/>Disruption scenarios, exposure,<br/>service loss, vulnerability"]
    P3 --> P4["Paper 4<br/>Operations, DBN, recovery,<br/>resilience"]
    OPS[("Anonymous request<br/>tickets (QR)")] --> P4
  • Paper 1 builds the baseline: group-specific accessibility, capacity, estimated demand, supply and Service Gap, with a BBN, Monte Carlo uncertainty, sensitivity and what-if scenarios.
  • Paper 2 splits total need (Population × p) into visible and hidden need through a latent non-take-up node with parents Social Susceptibility, need-based gap, access deterrence and alternatives outside the network (OQ-8, OQ-10, OQ-11), giving Estimated Total Need.
  • Paper 3 runs simulated disruption scenarios and infers Vulnerability from Group Exposure, Service Loss and Social Susceptibility. It stops before resilience.
  • Paper 4 adds real operational data (anonymous tickets), facility and territorial functional state, a DBN, Bayesian updating of vulnerability, recovery trajectories and Resilience, plus per-facility operational output.

docs.title: 2. Indices and unit of analysis
docs.text:
Notation decided in OQ-1 (the papers' original symbols differ; see paper-revisions.md).

Symbol Meaning i spatial unit. First application: Local Community, Greek ΤΚ (Τοπική Κοινότητα). The code must stay generic. Demand, supply and gap belong to i f facility; travel time is T_if^{g,m} g population group s service m transport mode: walking, public transport, car c scenario (counterfactual or disruption) t time l state of a discrete variable, as in Σ_l P(X = l) … k, p, τ intensity (OQ-24), need prevalence and take-up (OQ-8)

Unit of analysis (Paper 4 §3): spatial unit × social group × service × time. The state of one facility is never automatically the state of a spatial unit: a facility can be degraded while the unit stays covered by alternatives.

Three kinds of need (OQ-8, decided). Hidden need: need never expressed (Paper 2). Unmet expressed need: requests not fulfilled within the maximum acceptable waiting time (Service Gap, Paper 1; Service Loss, Paper 3). Met need: requests fulfilled. They never overlap, so no unmet need is counted twice.

Units of measurement (OQ-24, decided). Need, capacity, supply, gap and loss are measured in service units per reference period (visits, appointments or hours, defined per service). Need is people with need × intensity. Quantities of different services are never summed. The reference period is open (OQ-25). A request not fulfilled within the service's maximum acceptable waiting time counts as unmet (OQ-26).

docs.title: 3. Entities
docs.text:
• SpatialUnit: id, geometry, population by group.
  • PopulationGroup: id, definition rule (for example Age ≥ 65, Income < T), and three profiles: demographic (how many people), mobility (how they can travel), demand (how likely they need the service). Examples: Elderly, Mobility-limited, Unemployed, Low-income. Groups may overlap (OQ-6). A group is not a measure of need.
  • Service: a type of social service, with its own service unit (visit, appointment, hour) and maximum acceptable waiting time (OQ-24, OQ-26).
  • Facility: location, type, services offered, capacity inputs (places, staff, throughput), operating hours, operational status, availability.
  • TransportMode and per-mode Network (road, pedestrian, public transport) plus DEM.
  • Scenario: a set of changes relative to the baseline (an overlay, never a copy of the data): what-if interventions (Paper 1 §13, for example capacity +20 %, new facility) and disruptions (Paper 3: facility severities DS ∈ [0,1] with 0 none, 0.25 minor, 0.5 moderate, 0.75 severe, 1 complete; closed network edges), plus rationing case (OQ-24) and a reference-scenario flag (OQ-16). Stored as versioned, schema-validated JSON with an owner and visibility (private, shared).
  • Run: one immutable execution of a scenario. Records everything needed to reproduce it: scenario version, data package version, code version (git commit), model and parameter version (CPTs, priors), random seed, configuration. Lifecycle queued → running → succeeded | failed | cancelled, with progress. Identical inputs may reuse results.
  • Result: belongs to one run. Summary values per unit × group × service (probabilities, intervals) in the database for maps; full Monte Carlo samples in Parquet files.
  • Study area: one or more core municipalities plus a buffer of neighbouring units (OQ-28).
  • Onboarding: the hub keeps national raw sources (boundaries, network, population, DEM) as versioned files and processes them only for onboarded study areas (clip with buffer, clean, checks, DP-NNN notes). Thematic layers (facilities, services, capacities, transit, susceptibility indicators) are added per municipality, incrementally, through validated imports. Each municipality has an onboarding status and a coverage matrix (layer × status: missing, open data, estimated, verified).
  • Stable identifiers and history: every unit, facility, node and edge keeps the same id across packages and installations; features carry municipality_id, role (core | buffer), quality and valid_from/valid_to (closed, never deleted).
  • Data package: a versioned (semantic versioning), checksummed bundle for one study area plus a buffer, with layer coverage, changelog and provenance, produced by the hub and imported by an installation after a preview of changes. When a municipality is onboarded or corrected, the hub publishes new versions of the packages of every study area whose buffer includes it.
  • Deployment: the same code runs as a municipal installation (it serves one study area of one or more core municipalities: its own users, scenarios, runs and tickets) or as the hub (raw sources, onboarding, curated data, packages, optional aggregated indicators shared upwards by municipalities).
  • Ticket: anonymous request (section 4.4).
  • RecoveryTrajectory: time series of service loss or observed consequence per (unit, group, service).

docs.title: 4. Variable catalogue
docs.text: Kinds: INPUT, PARAMETER (uncertain input), COMPUTED (simulation, not a BN node), EVIDENCE (computed outside the BN, fed in as evidence), BN-PARENT, BN-TARGET, LATENT, OBSERVED, OUTPUT. Formulas are as stated in the papers unless a decision in open-questions.md replaced them (marked with the OQ-n); open gaps are listed there. Notation follows OQ-1.

docs.title: 4.1 Paper 1: baseline
docs.text:
Variable As stated Kind Dimensions Population population by unit and group (ELSTAT) INPUT unit × group Demand rate DemandRate^g visible use: share of the group that reaches the service in the reference period, conceptually p × τ (OQ-8, OQ-24); from literature, statistics, expert elicitation. Not need prevalence PARAMETER group × service People making requests (Paper 1) Population × DemandRate, under average conditions. Not people with need, which is Population × p (Paper 2, OQ-8) COMPUTED unit × group × service Intensity k service units one person needs per reference period (OQ-24) PARAMETER group × service Estimated demand D_{i,g,s} people making requests × k, in service units per reference period (OQ-24, OQ-25). Labelled Estimated, never Observed COMPUTED unit × group × service Travel time T_if^{g,m} access time from unit i to facility f for group g, mode m COMPUTED unit × facility × group × mode Access weight w(T) converts time to a weight (form not given, OQ-3) COMPUTED Accessibility Accessibility_i^{g,m} built from w(T_if^{g,m}) (combination of modes: OQ-5) COMPUTED Physical capacity C_f^physical from places, staff, throughput, and so on INPUT/PARAMETER facility Availability availability of the facility PARAMETER facility Functional capacity C_f^functional C_f^physical × Availability_f COMPUTED facility Effective capacity ~~C_ij^effective = C_i^functional × w(T_ij)~~ (original notation) replaced by 2SFCA allocation (OQ-2, decided): each facility's functional capacity is shared among the units and groups that reach it, in proportion to access-weighted demand; shares sum to the facility's capacity COMPUTED facility × unit × group Supply S_{i,g,s} sum of the 2SFCA shares a unit and group receive from all facilities (OQ-2) COMPUTED unit × group × service Service Gap SG_{i,g,s} max(0, D − S): unmet expressed need (OQ-8); ratio SG/D; states LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH with documented thresholds (relation to the BBN: OQ-4) COMPUTED + BN node unit × group × service

BBN (Paper 1 §9): Population group → Demand; Accessibility; Infrastructure → Physical capacity → Functional capacity → Effective supply → Service Gap. Supply-related nodes stay explicit and are not hidden inside Service Gap, so the network can explain why a gap is high (low capacity, low accessibility or high demand). CPTs are initialised from expert elicitation, literature and deterministic relations of the service model.

docs.title: 4.2 Paper 2: hidden need
docs.text:
Variable As stated Kind Dimensions Group characteristics indicators not already used in the group definition (household dependency and composition, living alone, employment stability, 80+, mobility indicators) INPUT unit × group Social Susceptibility SS_{i,g,s} propensity of a group to experience unmet or insufficient provision of a service due to its characteristics, independently of current availability, accessibility or capacity. States Low / Medium / High. Indicators may differ by service; group-definition variables never reused (OQ-9, decided) BN-PARENT unit × group × service Need-based gap max(0, Population × p × k − Supply): shortfall of Paper 1 supply relative to total need, not to current users. Replaces reuse of Paper 1 Service Gap, which would create a loop through take-up (OQ-10, decided) EVIDENCE unit × group × service Access deterrence accessibility only as a direct deterrent to seeking the service, for example travel time to the nearest facility offering it. Not capacity reaching the unit, which is in the need-based gap (OQ-11, decided) EVIDENCE unit × group × service Alternatives outside the network options not among modelled facilities (private services, family, NGOs, parishes); expert estimates where no data (OQ-11, decided). Alternative facilities in the network are already in the need-based gap EVIDENCE unit × group × service Need prevalence p share of the group that needs the service in the reference period; from data if available, otherwise experts (OQ-8) PARAMETER unit × group × service Non-take-up level (the Hidden Need node) latent; P(state | SS, need-based gap, access deterrence, outside alternatives), no edges among the parents (OQ-11); states are ranges of 1 − τ, for example Low 0–20 %, Medium 20–50 %, High 50–80 % (OQ-8, OQ-10; edges OQ-11). CPT learned from observed use (parameter learning, pooled across units) LATENT unit × group × service Take-up τ share of people with need who express it (make a request), whether or not they are served; sampled within the posterior state ranges in Monte Carlo (OQ-8) COMPUTED unit × group × service Hidden need (people) need never expressed: Population × p × (1 − τ); share of group = p × (1 − τ), reported with an interval and with sensitivity to p OUTPUT unit × group × service Visible need (people) Population × p × τ. Used for aggregate calibration where aggregate figures exist; the ratio to Paper 1 demand is a descriptive indicator only (OQ-8) COMPUTED unit × group × service Observed use requests from administrative records or tickets; evidence for learning take-up, only from facilities with known recording coverage (OQ-8) OBSERVED unit × group × service × period Estimated Total Need ETN Population × p × k in service units (OQ-8, OQ-24); replaces EstimatedDemand + E(HiddenNeed) OUTPUT unit × group × service

CPTs come from expert elicitation by comparing scenarios (for example Low SS, Low gap, high accessibility, many alternatives against High SS, Low gap, low accessibility, few alternatives). Counterfactuals here serve uncertainty, sensitivity and robustness, not estimation.

docs.title: 4.3 Paper 3: disruption and vulnerability
docs.text:
Variable As stated Kind Need Pressure NP ETN / BaselineAvailableService. Descriptive baseline indicator. Decision: not a parent of Vulnerability (double counting risk); used for characterisation, sensitivity, optional covariate COMPUTED Disruption severity DS_{f,c} scenario parameter in [0,1] PARAMETER (not a BN node) Disrupted capacity C^D_f = C_f (1 − DS_f) COMPUTED Disrupted network, accessibility Network^D, then accessibility recomputed from Network^D, DEM, population COMPUTED Group Exposure GE AffectedPopulation / Population_{i,g} per group (no separate population, infrastructure or network exposure nodes) EVIDENCE Baseline available service AS⁰ available service without disruption COMPUTED Disrupted available service ASᴰ f(Capacity^D, Accessibility^D) (OQ-14). No adaptive redistribution or alternative activation here (Paper 4) COMPUTED Baseline gap PUN⁰ max(0, ETN − AS⁰), need unmet before any disruption (OQ-12) COMPUTED Potential Unmet Need PUNᴰ max(0, ETN − ASᴰ) COMPUTED Disruption loss ΔPUN PUNᴰ − PUN⁰, always stored in absolute service units (OQ-12, OQ-24) COMPUTED / OUTPUT Service Loss SL (PUNᴰ − PUN⁰) / ETN, in [0,1], 0 when nothing changes (OQ-12, decided; replaces the paper's PUN / ETN). Not latent, not Vulnerability, not Resilience EVIDENCE Relative Service Loss SL′ (PUNᴰ − PUN⁰) / min(ETN, AS⁰), secondary indicator, not a BN node (OQ-12) OUTPUT Rationing uniform or concentrated, bounding how shortage is spread among people (OQ-24) PARAMETER (scenario) Breadth, depth, severity of loss per-person loss indicators in the Foster–Greer–Thorbecke style, computed for each rationing case, not BN nodes (OQ-24) OUTPUT Social Susceptibility SS_{i,g,s} from Paper 2, not recomputed (OQ-9) BN-PARENT Vulnerability relationship the CPT P(V | GE, SL, SS): how a disruption turns into consequences for a group (OQ-16, decided). States Low / Medium / High (OQ-15). Expert elicitation first; no ad hoc weighted average BN-TARGET (CPT) Vulnerability at a scenario V_{i,g,s,c} the relationship evaluated at scenario c; run separately per group. Mapped at reference scenarios (minor, moderate, severe) so areas compare at the same intensity OUTPUT Risk vulnerability averaged over scenarios weighted by their probability of occurrence. Not vulnerability; produced only if disruption probabilities exist (OQ-16) OUTPUT (future)

Two layers: Layer 1 is computational (scenario, disruption, simulation, evidence). Layer 2 is Bayesian inference over the three parents. Monte Carlo samples uncertain parameters, runs the simulation, infers, stores, and yields P(V = High) rather than a score.

docs.title: 4.4 Paper 4: operations, dynamics, resilience
docs.text:
Variable As stated Kind Ticket anonymous request: spatial unit, group (overlap rule: OQ-6), service/need, facility where the request is made or scheduled (OQ-29), request time t_r, scheduled time t_a, service time t_f, expiry t_e, and a flag "first request in this period" (yes/no, no identifier) to count people without identifying them (OQ-8, OQ-21) OBSERVED Recording coverage share of a facility's requests captured by the ticket system, per facility and period; observations are used for learning only where coverage is full or known (OQ-8) OBSERVED Operational indicators demand rate, waiting time, fulfilment delay, appointment adherence, overdue requests, expired requests, service coverage, unfulfilled need COMPUTED Facility functional state Normal → Under Pressure → Degraded → Critical → Recovering → Normal, from operational indicators LATENT/STATE Need for support, resource mobilisation response mechanism, approved and controlled volunteer resources included; not an independent "community resilience" measure STATE Network redundancy, territorial (ΤΚ) service coverage and functional state combine facility coverages and redundancy STATE Observed exposure and loss GE(t), SL(t) derived from territorial functional state and tickets, using the same definitions as Paper 3 (OQ-12, OQ-16) COMPUTED Expected group consequence the Paper 3 vulnerability relationship evaluated at observed GE(t), SL(t) and SS. The disruption enters once (OQ-16) COMPUTED Observed group consequence from total need, covered need, unfulfilled need in tickets; linked to latent V by a measurement node P(ObservedConsequence | V) (OQ-18) OBSERVED Updated vulnerability relationship Bayesian parameter learning of the CPT, with the expert CPT as prior (for example Dirichlet per row). Weight of prior against data: OQ-27 BN update Recovery trajectory ServiceLoss(t) or ObservedGroupConsequence(t) OBSERVED series Resilience P(Resilience_{unit,g,s} | trajectory) indicators: maximum loss, recovery time, recovery rate, cumulative impact (AUC), final restoration level OUTPUT Facility operational output functional state, coverage, pending requests, resource need by type (for example medical, administrative, transport) OUTPUT

DBN (Paper 4 §12): State(t−1) → FunctionalState(t) → ObservedConsequence(t) → Response(t) → Recovery(t) → State(t+1), in parallel with Vulnerability → ExpectedConsequence → ObservedConsequence. Since OQ-16, the parallel branch is: observed GE(t), SL(t) and SS → vulnerability relationship → Expected Consequence, compared with Observed Consequence to learn the relationship's parameters. Exact topology and time slice: OQ-17.

docs.title: 5. Cross-cutting machinery (shared by all papers)
docs.text:
• Discrete Bayesian modelling: ordinal variables, CPTs, elicitation from expert scenarios, inference. Engine choice via ADR.
  • Monte Carlo uncertainty: sample uncertain inputs and CPT parameters, run the model, collect P(·) or a distribution (Paper 1 §11, Paper 2 §14, Paper 3 §22).
  • Sensitivity: rank factors by influence (Paper 1 §12, Paper 2 §16, Paper 3 §23).
  • Scenarios: controlled interventions (Paper 1 §13, for example capacity +20 %, staff +1, new facility, accessibility −20 %) and disruption scenarios (Paper 3 §7–10). One shared engine.
  • Validation: expert validation, plausibility and monotonicity checks, sensitivity; later calibration against observed data (Papers 1–3 §14/18/24).
  • Alternative allocation models (future, see OQ-2 notes N-2a, N-2b): 3SFCA as a candidate refinement, and capacity-constrained allocation as an alternative model for sensitivity analysis only. The baseline is 2SFCA. The capacity module should expose allocation behind an interface so these can be added without changing callers.

docs.title: 7. Invariants
docs.text: See the root AGENTS.md ("Domain invariants"). The most important: keep BN nodes, computed simulation variables and scenario parameters separate (section 4); never mix vulnerability and resilience; never treat estimated demand as total need.

Issues found while turning Papers 1–4 into a model. None of these may be resolved in code. Implementation tickets that depend on one are labelled needs-spec. Each question becomes a research-question or adr issue. Reference them in code and docs as OQ-n.
