docs.title: User guide: getting started
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0. Screenshots come from the UAT walk-through on synthetic data (UAT 01); a few labels may differ slightly from your screen.

This guide is for the people who use SolidarityNode in a municipality: analysts who write scenarios and run them, viewers who read shared results, and administrators who manage users and data. No technical background is needed. For the ideas behind the screens (data package, scenario, run, data version), read Concepts first.

No research results yet

Every result in version 0.1.0 comes from the diagnostic model (διαγνωστικό μοντέλο), which only checks that the platform works. Every page that shows results says so in a yellow banner. See the FAQ.

docs.title: Open the platform
docs.text:
Your installation has an address given by your administrator. On a test machine, after make uat, it is http://127.0.0.1:8080 (UAT guide).

  1. Open the address and sign in.
  2. The Study area page opens: the map of your data (Study area).
  3. Use the menu at the top: Study area, Scenarios, Admin (administrators only), Health.
  4. Switch the Language between English and Ελληνικά at any time; Greek terms follow the glossary.

The footer of every page names the build you are using: licence, the active data version, the backend version with its git commit and environment, and the frontend commit. Quote it when you report a problem.

docs.title: A typical session
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    L["Sign in"] --> SA["Study area<br/>look at the data"]
    SA --> SL["Scenarios<br/>open or create"]
    SL --> ED["Scenario editor<br/>describe the changes, save"]
    ED --> RUN["Run<br/>progress, then results"]
    RUN --> CMP["Compare<br/>with the baseline"]
    RUN --> EXP["Export<br/>CSV or GeoPackage"]

docs.title: Pages of this guide
docs.text: Screen What you do there Who Signing in sign in, sign out, what happens after wrong passwords everyone Study area see units, facilities and roads, data quality and coverage everyone Scenarios list find your scenarios and shared ones, their latest runs everyone Scenario editor write a "what if", validate and save versions analysts, administrators Run follow a run, read results with uncertainty, export everyone (viewers: shared scenarios) Compare compare a run with the baseline or another data version everyone Admin users, data packages, results storage administrators Data packages and updates what happens when new data arrives everyone Roles who can do what everyone FAQ seed, reused runs, edge effect, diagnostic model everyone

docs.title: Admin
docs.text: Describes platform version 0.1.0. For administrators only; other users see "This page is for administrators."

docs.title: Data packages
docs.text:
• Active data: the data version that new scenarios and runs use.
  • Imported versions: every version ever imported. Earlier ones are kept for their runs; Make … active again goes back to one (rollback).
  • Packages available on the server, or upload a package archive (.zip, .tar.gz).
  • Preview shows, before anything is imported: whether it is new, an update or already imported; the changes per layer (added, changed, closed, unchanged features); coverage changes; the package changelog; and any validation problems (in English, since they quote file and column names).
  • Confirm import imports it in one step. The new version becomes active, a baseline run is queued, and scenarios that refer to closed or missing features are listed.

What this means for everyone else: Data packages and updates. From a terminal, the same actions are make import-package PKG=… and make activate-version VERSION=….

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• New user: username, password (at least 12 characters; common passwords are refused) and role (viewer, analyst, administrator).
  • Change a user's role or make them inactive. You cannot demote or disable yourself, and the last active administrator can never be demoted or disabled.
  • The first administrator of a new installation is created in a terminal with make create-admin.

Roles are explained in Roles.

docs.title: Results storage
docs.text: "N samples file(s) for N run(s): … MB; free on the results volume: … MB." Nothing is deleted automatically. Back up the database and the results volume together (a backup guide is not written yet; see the changelog).

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

On a succeeded run, Compare with baseline opens the Compare runs page: run A (yours) next to run B (the baseline, no changes).

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Three maps: A, B and Difference A − B.
  • One colour scale for A and B: a unit with the same value has the same colour on both maps.
  • The table gives "A: median (90 % interval)", "B: median (90 % interval)" and the difference of medians A − B. The difference is between the two central values; its own uncertainty is not computed yet (ADR 0017).
  • Uncertainty switches maps A and B to the width of their intervals, again with one scale.

docs.title: Which runs can be compared
docs.text:
• Two runs on the same data version: any two scenarios.
  • Two runs of the same scenario on different data versions: the page says "Same scenario across data versions 1.0.0 → 1.1.0." This shows what the data update changed.
  • Different scenarios on different data versions: refused, because the difference would mix two causes.

From a run page, Runs of this scenario → Compare with this run compares two runs of the same scenario.

docs.title: Data packages and updates
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0. From the user's point of view; the format is in ADR 0013.

The official data of your study area arrives as a data package (πακέτο δεδομένων), built by the hub from official and open sources, with a processing note for every step. An administrator imports it; analysts and viewers never upload data (Concepts).

docs.title: What happens on an update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor Admin as Administrator
    participant P as Platform
    actor A as Analysts and viewers
    Admin->>P: Preview package 1.1.0
    P-->>Admin: changes per layer, coverage, changelog (nothing imported yet)
    Admin->>P: Confirm import
    P->>P: 1.1.0 becomes active, 1.0.0 is kept
    P->>P: queue a baseline run on 1.1.0
    P->>P: check every scenario again against 1.1.0
    P-->>Admin: scenarios that need attention
    A->>P: open Scenarios, runs, Study area
    P-->>A: old runs unchanged, with "Rerun on data 1.1.0"
  1. Old runs never change. They keep showing the data they used, with a note and Rerun on data 1.1.0.
  2. Scenarios are checked again. One that names a feature that no longer exists (for example a closed facility) shows Needs attention and cannot run until it is edited.
  3. A baseline run on the new data is queued at once.
  4. In Scenarios, a scenario without a run on the new data shows Latest run on data 1.0.0.
  5. Compare two runs of the same scenario across the two data versions to see what the update changed (Compare).

docs.title: Going back
docs.text: An administrator can make an earlier version active again (Admin → Imported versions → Make … active again). The same things happen: a baseline run is queued, scenarios are checked again, nothing is deleted.

docs.title: If the data is wrong
docs.text: Do not work around it with a scenario. Send the correction to the hub (through your administrator): it arrives in the next package version, for every installation that uses it.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text: Describes platform version 0.1.0.

docs.title: Why does every result say "diagnostic model"?
docs.text: Because no research method is implemented yet. The only model, diagnostic-v0, computes simple things (travel times on the network after the scenario's changes, and random noise) to check that the platform works: scenarios are applied, runs are reproducible, uncertainty is stored and displayed, exports are complete. Its numbers are not accessibility, need, vulnerability or resilience, and every page says so. The research methods come paper by paper (roadmap); each needs its open questions decided first (open questions).

docs.title: What is the seed?
docs.text: Results come from Monte Carlo simulation: many random draws. The random seed (a whole number) fixes those draws, so the same run gives exactly the same numbers again. If you give none, the platform draws one and records it, so the run stays reproducible. Change the seed only to check that conclusions do not depend on one particular set of draws.

docs.title: Why did my run open at once, without computing?
docs.text:
The platform found a run with exactly the same inputs: the same scenario version, data version, code, model, seed and settings. A run never changes, so the existing one is the answer: it opens instead of computing again. A failed or cancelled run is never reused, and a run whose results file fails its integrity check is not reused either (the page says why).

To get a new run, change something that matters: a new scenario version, another seed, or new data.

docs.title: What is the edge effect?
docs.text: People near a municipal boundary often use facilities on the other side. The study area includes a buffer of neighbouring units for this reason. If a neighbouring municipality has no facility data, results for the units next to it may be biased (for example travel times that are too long). Those units get an orange outline and the warning "⚠ edge effect (OQ-28)" (φαινόμενο ορίου). The warning disappears when the hub adds the neighbour's facilities; how large the buffer should be is still an open question (OQ-28).

docs.title: Why is a result "Not reported" for some units?
docs.text: They are buffer units: they belong to a neighbouring municipality and are in the data only so that cross-boundary use is counted. Results are reported for your own (core) units only.

docs.title: Why are some changes "recorded only"?
docs.text: The scenario format can already hold changes that no method uses yet (disruption severities, travel-time changes, new roads, population changes). They are saved and shown, so nothing is lost, but they do not change results until the methods that use them exist (Scenario editor).

docs.title: Can I upload my own data?
docs.text: No. Data comes from the hub as data packages, imported by an administrator, so every installation uses checked data with known sources. To test a change, write a scenario; to correct the data, send the correction to the hub (Data packages and updates).

docs.title: Is any personal data stored?
docs.text: No. The platform holds synthetic or aggregated data only. The future operational data (anonymous request tickets) records only the area, group, service, facility and times, and nothing is stored until the privacy rules for small areas are decided (ADR 0010, OQ-21).

docs.title: Where do I report a problem?
docs.text: Tell your administrator, or open an issue on GitHub with the steps, what you expected, what you saw, and the build line from the footer. Never paste passwords or real personal data (UAT guide).

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

  1. Enter your username and password and press Log in.
  2. The Study area page opens. The header says "Signed in as name (role)", for example "Signed in as demo-analyst (analyst)".
  3. To leave, press Log out. A session ends by itself after some hours (12 by default).

Accounts are created by an administrator (Admin); there is no self-registration. Passwords have at least 12 characters, and common passwords are refused.

docs.title: Wrong password and locks
docs.text:
• A wrong username or password always gives the same message, "Wrong username or password.", so nobody can learn which usernames exist.
  • After several failures for one username, the next tries are delayed, and then the username is locked for about 15 minutes: "Too many failed sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again."
  • Failures for one username never lock out another username.
  • An administrator can clear a lock early (make clear-login-locks USERNAME=…, see the UAT guide).

Details and the reasons: ADR 0015.

docs.title: Demo accounts (test machines only)
docs.text: make uat creates demo-admin and demo-analyst, only when APP_ENV=development. Their passwords are public; they never exist on a real installation.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

Role Greek Can Viewer θεατής See shared scenarios and their runs: results, map, table, exports. Cannot create, edit or run scenarios. Analyst αναλυτής Everything a viewer can, plus create, edit, run, duplicate and share their own scenarios, and run the baseline. Administrator διαχειριστής Everything an analyst can, on every scenario (including other users' private ones), plus manage users, import data packages and choose the active data version. Hub (outside your installation) Builds and publishes data packages; receives corrections to the data. Planned for v0.2 (roadmap).

Private scenarios are visible to their owner and to administrators; shared scenarios to every user. A run inherits the visibility of its scenario: a run of a private scenario is "not found" for other users.

The same table, with the reasons, is in Concepts; the decision is ADR 0015.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

A run (εκτέλεση) computes one scenario version on one data version, in the background, and never changes afterwards (Concepts).

docs.title: Start a run
docs.text:
Open a scenario and click Run this version (or Run in the Scenarios list). Optional settings before you start:

  • Random seed: a number that fixes the random draws, so the run can be repeated exactly. Leave it empty and one is drawn and recorded (FAQ).
  • Pause after each step: slows the run down so that progress and cancelling can be followed (for testing).

Before it starts, the platform estimates the size of the results file and warns if it is large.

docs.title: Follow it
docs.text:
The Status goes queued → running (with a progress bar and "… % done") → succeeded, failed or cancelled. You can leave the page; the run continues.

  • Cancel run stops it at its next step: "Cancelled by a user while running." No results are kept.
  • If the worker stops during the run, it ends as failed with a message saying so; start the run again (a failed run is never reused).

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
1. The yellow banner: Diagnostic model: not a research result.
  2. Under Show, choose the Group, Service and Indicator.
  3. The map colours the core units; buffer units are grey ("Not reported"). Orange outlines mark the edge effect.
  4. The table gives, per unit, the value, the value Before the scenario, whether it Changed, and Warnings in words.

Uncertainty is always shown. A value is the median (διάμεσος) with its 90 % interval (διάστημα) in brackets, for example 0.05 (-1.6–1.7); the column heading says "Median (90 % interval)". Values that have no uncertainty say "(deterministic, no uncertainty)".

Map layers (both off by default):

  • Uncertainty: a second map, in blues, of the width of the 90 % interval;
  • Data quality: hatching for estimated data, dots for open data.

Below the table:

  • Hand-check of travel times: the diagnostic travel times are checked against hand-computed values from the data package.
  • What changed per unit: each change of the scenario, in words.
  • Recorded, no effect yet: changes the platform keeps but does not apply yet (Scenario editor).

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The Reproducibility section lists everything needed to repeat the run: scenario and version, data package and version, code version (git commit), model and version, random seed, configuration, input hash, the checksum of the samples file, and the environment that executed it (platform, Python and NumPy versions). An orange note appears when the code had local changes (-dirty): such a run can be repeated only on the machine that made it. Details: ADR 0017.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
• Export CSV: a zip with results.csv (median, interval, mean), travel times, per-unit changes and metadata.json with every reproducibility field.
  • Export GeoPackage: a results layer of unit polygons, for QGIS or other GIS software.

docs.title: After a data update
docs.text:
A run keeps the data it used. If the active data is newer, the page says "This run used data 1.0.0; the active data is 1.1.0." and offers Rerun on data 1.1.0, which makes a new run. Runs of this scenario lists every run, with Compare with this run.

A viewer sees the same page without the Run, Rerun and Cancel buttons:

docs.title: Scenario editor
docs.text: Describes platform version 0.1.0. For analysts and administrators.

docs.title: Write a scenario
docs.text:
1. Scenarios → New scenario.
  2. Type a Name (required) and, if useful, a Description.
  3. Choose the Visibility: private (you and administrators) or shared (every user, including viewers).
  4. Describe the changes, by clicking on the map or using Facilities and edges (text list):
    • Close an edge: click a road segment; it turns orange and dashed. Tick the transport modes it is closed for (walking, car). Segments that cannot be closed say so.
    • Disruption severity DS of a facility: select it and type a value from 0 (none) to 1 (complete), for example 0.5 (moderate).
    • Capacity change: choose a service, an input (places, staff, throughput), percent of baseline or absolute amount, and the amount; Add change.
  5. A scenario with a disruption must state its Rationing case (OQ-24) (for example uniform).
  6. Watch Validation: it says "The scenario is valid for the active data." or lists what is wrong; Save stays grey until the scenario is valid.
  7. Save: "Saved as version 1." Each later Save as new version keeps the earlier versions, so every run can say exactly which version it used.

Changes relative to the baseline lists everything the scenario changes, in words.

docs.title: What has an effect today
docs.text:
The diagnostic model applies closed edges and capacity changes. Other changes are recorded only (καταγράφεται μόνο): saved, listed and shown on the run page, with no effect on results yet:

  • the disruption severity of a facility (no method turns it into lost capacity yet);
  • changes of travel time or speed, new edges, population changes (they have no fields in the editor yet; scenarios that contain them keep them when you save).

When a scenario combines interventions and disruptions, the platform applies the interventions first and the disruptions after. This is a proposed default, not yet confirmed by the method (OQ-30; order in Lifecycles).

docs.title: Data version
docs.text: A scenario is created against one data version ("Version 1, created against data 1.0.0, owner demo-analyst"). A run always uses the active data; when they differ, the page says so next to Run this version. See Data packages and updates.

docs.title: Scenarios list
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

A scenario (σενάριο) is a "what if": a list of changes on top of the data (Concepts). The Scenarios page lists every scenario you may see.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• My scenarios: the scenarios you own (analysts and administrators). New scenario opens the editor.
  • Shared scenarios: scenarios every user may see, including Baseline (no changes), owned by "system".
  • Private scenarios of other users (administrators only): each marked "private (owner name)".

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
• Visibility: private (owner and administrators) or shared (every user, viewers included).
  • Latest run: the status of the latest run and a link to it:
    • "succeeded (1.1.0)": the latest run, on data 1.1.0;
    • Latest run on data 1.0.0: the scenario has no run on the active data yet;
    • Not run yet: never run. A viewer sees "Ask an analyst to run it."
  • Needs attention with the current data: the scenario names something that no longer exists in the active data (for example a closed facility). It has no Run button until it is edited. See Data packages and updates.
  • Run: runs the latest version on the active data. If an identical run exists, it opens instead (FAQ).

docs.title: Study area
docs.text:
Describes platform version 0.1.0.

The Study area page shows the active data version (ενεργή έκδοση δεδομένων): the spatial units, facilities and road network that new scenarios and runs use.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Header line: data package, version and date, for example "Data package demo-study-area-a, version 1.0.0 (2026-11-24). Synthetic data."
  • Map:
    • core units (solid outline) belong to your municipality; results are reported for them;
    • buffer units (grey, dashed) belong to neighbouring municipalities; they are there so that people served across the boundary are counted, and no results are reported for them;
    • facilities (dots) and network edges (lines);
    • quality patterns: hatched = estimated, dotted = open data, plain = verified by the municipality;
    • orange outline: edge-effect warning (FAQ);
    • a closed facility stays on the map, white with a dashed ring, for history.
  • Selected feature: click a unit, facility or edge on the map (or in Features (text list)) to see its details: municipality, role (core or buffer), quality, valid from and to, and for facilities the services with their capacity inputs (places, staff, throughput).
  • Legend: every symbol in words.
  • Data coverage per municipality and layer: for each municipality and layer (boundaries, population, network, facilities, public transport) whether data is verified, open data, estimated or missing.
  • Package changelog and the processing notes (DP-NNN) behind the data, and Licences and attribution per layer.

docs.title: Keyboard and language
docs.text:
• Press Tab until the map has a blue focus frame, then use the arrow keys and + / - to pan and zoom.
  • Every map item is also in Features (text list), so nothing needs a mouse.
  • Ελληνικά: the same page in Greek ("φαινόμενο ορίου" for the edge effect).

docs.title: After a data update
docs.text:
When an administrator imports a new data version, this page shows it at once. In the demo, version 1.1.0 adds facility F4 in the neighbouring municipality (so the edge-effect warning disappears) and closes F3.

More: Data packages and updates.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning (while 0.x, see docs/releasing.md).

Every pull request that changes behaviour adds a line under Unreleased (AGENTS.md). Each release section also states known limitations and upgrade notes for installations.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text: Nothing yet.

docs.title: 0.1.0 - unreleased
docs.text: First version: the platform foundation of a municipal installation, on synthetic data, with the diagnostic model only. Pull requests #1 (bootstrap), #3 (AGENTS.md), #4 (CI), #5 (OQ-29), #6 (platform mechanics) and the documentation site.

docs.title: Added: for users
docs.text:
• Sign-in and roles: local accounts (administrator, analyst, viewer); passwords of at least 12 characters, common passwords refused; sign-in throttling with delays and temporary locks; the last active administrator is always kept (ADR 0015).
  • Study area on a map (Leaflet): core and buffer units, facilities and network; data quality on every feature (verified by the municipality, open data, estimated); coverage per municipality and layer; edge-effect warnings for units next to a neighbour without facility data (OQ-28, warning only); keyboard navigation and a text list of every feature.
  • Scenarios: versioned "what if" overlays built on the map (close an edge per mode, facility disruption severity, capacity changes in percent or absolute amounts), validated against the active data, private or shared; network and population changes accepted as recorded-only placeholders (ADR 0016).
  • Runs in the background with progress and cancel; every run immutable and reproducible (scenario version, data version, code version, model and version, seed, configuration, environment); identical inputs reuse the earlier run (ADR 0017).
  • Results by spatial unit, group and service with the median and a 90 % interval everywhere, an optional uncertainty map and data-quality layer; comparison with the baseline or across data versions of one scenario (one shared colour scale, difference of medians); export to CSV and GeoPackage with the reproducibility metadata.
  • Data packages (ADR 0013): preview of changes, checksums, import in one transaction, every version kept, rollback to an earlier version (Admin screen, make import-package, make activate-version); after an update, a baseline run is queued and every scenario revalidated; old runs offer Rerun on data X.
  • English and Greek interface, with the terms of docs/i18n/glossary.md; the footer names the build (backend version and commit, frontend commit, data version).
  • docs/concepts.md for municipal staff; UAT checklists docs/uat/00-bootstrap.md and docs/uat/01-platform.md with screenshots.

docs.title: Added: technical
docs.text:
• Monorepo: core (Python 3.12, typed domain model and module interfaces, no web or database dependencies), backend (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, PostGIS), frontend (React, TypeScript, Vite), docs, synthetic data, Makefile; Podman by default, Docker supported (ADR 0001, 0011).
  • core: domain model indexed by spatial unit × social group × service × time (ADR 0003), uncertain values, variable catalogue, model registry, scenario overlay with the order of application (OQ-30, proposed), summary statistics of samples, and the diagnostic model diagnostic-v0 0.2.1 (labelled "Diagnostic model: not a research result").
  • backend: PostgreSQL job queue and worker service with heartbeat lease, cancel and optional maximum runtime (ADR 0006); results summaries in PostGIS and Monte Carlo samples in Parquet with SHA-256 (ADR 0008); deployment role municipality | hub locked in the database (ADR 0012); anonymous ticket schema with the facility field (OQ-29), nothing stored (ADR 0010); scenario JSON Schema and OpenAPI exported to docs/schemas/ (make schemas); server messages with stable codes translated by the UI.
  • Operations: make setup, up, uat, reset, seed, check-config (refuses placeholder secrets in production), create-admin, db-shell, clear-login-locks; APP_ENV; /health, /health/ready, /version.
  • Synthetic demo dataset (DP-001) and demo packages 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 (DP-002), generated by scripts.
  • Quality: ruff, mypy strict, ESLint, Prettier, Vitest, pytest, Playwright end-to-end test in a throw-away stack; CI per component, image builds with Podman and Docker, licence check, DCO check, Dependabot.
  • Governance: AGPL-3.0-or-later, AGENTS.md rules for every contributor and coding agent, contributing guide, code of conduct, security and trademark policies, ADRs 0001–0017, open questions OQ-1 to OQ-30.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Documentation site (MkDocs with the Material theme, versioned with mike, published to GitHub Pages): user guide with one page per screen, roles and FAQ; architecture pages per component with Mermaid diagrams of the run lifecycle, run statuses, data update flow, data model and scenario application order; roadmap; release process (make docs, make docs-build).
  • Generated and CI-checked: the ADR index, the specifications index, the open-question counts (make docs-generate) and the dependency and licence report docs/architecture/dependencies.md (make deps-report); link checking of the README and docs.
  • The platform version has one source, the file VERSION (make version, make version-sync, checked by make lint), and the run reproducibility record names it (environment.solidaritynode, not in the input hash).
  • README as a short landing page; CITATION.cff; milestones per roadmap step and labels paper:1 … paper:4.
  • Rules: diagrams are Mermaid and change with the behaviour they describe; every PR that changes behaviour adds a line under Unreleased and updates the user guide page it affects.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Diagnostic model only. No research method is implemented; results check the platform and are not accessibility, need, vulnerability or resilience.
  • No hub onboarding yet. Only the municipal installation is complete; data packages are imported by hand (roadmap step 2).
  • OpenStreetMap tiles are for development only. Light interactive use within the OSMF tile usage policy; use SOLIDARITYNODE_BASEMAP=blank offline or for any heavier use, until a tile source for production is chosen.
  • No backup guide yet. The database and the results volume must be backed up together; nothing is deleted automatically.
  • Disruption severities, network and population changes are recorded only, with no effect on results.
  • No request tickets are stored until the privacy rules are decided (OQ-21, ADR 0010).
  • Synthetic data only.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text: • First release: install from scratch (make setup, then make up and make create-admin, or make uat for a test machine). Runs queued before an upgrade fail with "Start the run again".

docs.title: Contributing to SolidarityNode
docs.text:
Thank you for your interest. SolidarityNode is early-stage research software: code, methodological review, documentation and synthetic test data are all welcome.

By participating you agree to the Code of Conduct. Report security issues privately as described in SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read, in this order:

  1. AGENTS.md: domain invariants, architecture rules and conventions. They apply to every contributor, human or AI (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents all read this file).
  2. Also read the AGENTS.md of the folder you work in (core/, backend/, frontend/, data-processing/). The root file always applies; if the two conflict, the root wins and the conflict should be reported.
  3. The same area rules with short explanations and examples are in docs/conventions/.
  4. CLAUDE.md files only import AGENTS.md for Claude Code; they never contain rules.
  5. docs/specs/README.md: how the specification is organised.
  6. docs/specs/00-domain-model.md and docs/specs/open-questions.md.
  7. docs/architecture.md.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Requirements: git, make, uv, Node.js 26 with pnpm 12, and Podman (default) or Docker for the full stack.

make setup        # check tools, create .env if missing, install locked dependencies
make test-db      # once per session: PostGIS for the backend tests (or keep `make up` running)
make lint test    # must pass before every commit (unit and integration tests, no containers)
make test-e2e     # end-to-end test in a throw-away stack; also runs in CI on every PR
make up           # start db, backend and frontend (Podman by default)
make down

make setup names any missing tool (uv, node, pnpm); install it and open a new login shell so it is on PATH. No manual editing of .env is needed for development.

With Docker instead of Podman:

CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker COMPOSE="docker compose" make up

make help lists all targets. Optional local hooks: uvx pre-commit install.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All configuration comes from .env (git-ignored), created by make setup from .env.example. make setup also warns when .env lacks a key that .env.example defines. Defaults are safe for local development; secrets are change-me placeholders, which the backend refuses when APP_ENV is anything other than development or test (check with make check-config APP_ENV=production). Production values are never committed.

Setting Used by Default Meaning POSTGRES_DB db, backend solidaritynode Database name POSTGRES_USER db, backend solidaritynode Database user POSTGRES_PASSWORD db, backend change-me Database password (secret) DB_HOST_PORT compose 5432 Host port for PostgreSQL, bound to 127.0.0.1 BACKEND_HOST_PORT compose, Makefile 8000 Host port for the API, bound to 127.0.0.1 FRONTEND_HOST_PORT compose, Makefile 8080 Host port for the frontend, bound to 127.0.0.1 APP_ENV backend development development, test (test suite) or production; outside development and test, placeholder secrets are refused SOLIDARITYNODE_LOG_LEVEL backend info debug, info, warning or error SOLIDARITYNODE_DATABASE_URL backend on the host built from POSTGRES_* in compose SQLAlchemy URL (secret) SOLIDARITYNODE_CORS_ORIGINS backend ["http://localhost:5173"] Origins allowed to call the API directly DEPLOYMENT_MODE backend, worker, CLI municipality municipality or hub (ADR 0012). Stored in the database at first initialisation; the backend refuses to start if it later differs. Only the municipal installation is complete in v0.1 SOLIDARITYNODE_BASEMAP backend → frontend osm Map background: osm (OpenStreetMap tiles, attributed, needs internet) or blank (offline) SOLIDARITYNODE_DIAGNOSTIC_STEP_DELAY_S runs 0.5 Pause after each progress step so progress and cancel can be followed; recorded in the run configuration SOLIDARITYNODE_SESSION_HOURS backend 12 Login session lifetime SOLIDARITYNODE_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE backend false Session cookie only over HTTPS; must be true with APP_ENV=production (the backend and make check-config refuse otherwise) SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES_ACCOUNT backend 5 Failed sign-ins for one username before it is locked (ADR 0015) SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES_ADDRESS backend 20 Failed sign-ins from one client address before it is locked SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_LOCK_MINUTES backend 15 Lock duration; failures older than this are forgotten SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_DELAY_BASE_S, SOLIDARITYNODE_LOGIN_DELAY_MAX_S backend 1, 30 After failure n the next attempt for that username waits base × 2^(n-1) seconds, at most the maximum; an address is delayed the same way from half its limit on SOLIDARITYNODE_TRUSTED_PROXIES backend loopback and private networks Reverse proxies whose X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For give the client address for sign-in throttling (the bundled nginx overwrites both); other peers' headers are ignored. A proxy address reported as client means the address is unknown: per-username limits only SOLIDARITYNODE_RESULTS_DIR backend, worker on the host var/results (/data/results volume in compose) Per-sample Parquet results and package uploads SOLIDARITYNODE_PACKAGES_DIR backend data/synthetic/packages Data packages offered for import on the Admin screen SOLIDARITYNODE_WORKER_NAME worker worker Worker name, for logs and the job row only SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS worker 10 How often the worker renews the lease (jobs.heartbeat_at) of the running job SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_STALE_SECONDS worker 120 A running job without a heartbeat for this long is failed by any worker ("Interrupted … Start the run again."); at least twice the heartbeat SOLIDARITYNODE_RESULT_INTERVAL_QUANTILES backend, worker 0.05,0.95 Quantile levels of the interval stored with every result (with the mean and the median); recorded in the run configuration and its input hash (ADR 0017) SOLIDARITYNODE_SAMPLES_WARN_MB backend 500 Warn when a run's samples file is estimated, before the run starts, above this many megabytes (ADR 0008); the run is still queued SOLIDARITYNODE_JOB_MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS worker empty (no limit) Optional maximum runtime per job kind, as kind=seconds pairs (for example run=3600); a job over it is stopped at its next progress step and marked failed SOLIDARITYNODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL backend tests compose db on 127.0.0.1:5432 PostGIS server on which the tests create a throw-away database GIT_COMMIT image builds set by make up Build identity shown by /version and the footer, recorded on every run; with APP_ENV=production it must be known and not end in -dirty (backend and worker refuse to start otherwise) CONTAINER_ENGINE, COMPOSE Makefile podman, podman compose Container engine and compose command

Adding a setting: add it to .env.example in the same PR with a safe development default (secrets as change-me) and a one-line comment, and add a row to this table (AGENTS.md, "Configuration").

docs.title: Testing by hand (UAT)
docs.text: The maintainer tests every PR by hand before merging. make uat gives a fresh, seeded environment and prints the URLs to open; see docs/uat/README.md. Every PR fills in the "How to test (UAT)" section of the template with numbered steps and expected results, and every feature ticket has an "Acceptance test (UAT)" section. Failed UAT is reported as a PR comment and the uat-failed label.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. One ticket, one branch, one PR. Branch name: feat/<issue-number>-short-name (or fix/…, docs/…, chore/…).
  2. Read the issue fully, including acceptance criteria and the linked spec section.
  3. If anything is ambiguous or the spec is silent, do not invent methodology: comment on the issue with the question and stop (see below).
  4. Implement in small commits and add tests that cover every acceptance criterion. Use synthetic data only.
  5. Update docs and the spec cross-reference if behaviour changed.
  6. Run make lint test, open a PR with the template and reference the issue (Closes #N). Do not merge your own PR.

docs.title: Paper issues
docs.text: Every issue that belongs to a paper carries both the label paper:N and the field Paper of the Kintsugi project with the same value (for example paper:2 and Paper = P2 Hidden need), and the paper's milestone (v0.3 Paper 1 Accessibility, v0.4 Paper 2 Hidden need, v0.5 Paper 3 Vulnerability, v0.6 Paper 4 Resilience). Reason: labels make the issue search links in the README and the roadmap work; the field drives the project views. If they disagree, fix the one that is wrong.

docs.title: Commits and DCO sign-off
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, test:, refactor:, chore:), and sign off every commit:

git commit -s -m "feat(core): add travel time interface"

The sign-off certifies the Developer Certificate of Origin: you wrote the change or have the right to submit it under the project licence (AGPL-3.0). The dco CI check rejects PRs with unsigned commits. Commits by Dependabot are exempt, since it cannot sign off. To fix the last commit: git commit --amend -s --no-edit; for several: git rebase --signoff main.

docs.title: Documentation and changelog
docs.text:
• Every PR that changes behaviour adds a line under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md and updates the user guide page it affects (docs/user-guide/). Reason: users read the guide and the release notes, not the diff.
  • Diagrams are Mermaid code blocks, updated in the same PR as the change they describe. Reason: they render on GitHub and on the site, and they can be reviewed as text.
  • Link instead of copying: issues and plans live in GitHub (Kintsugi), decisions in docs/adr/, open questions in docs/specs/open-questions.md.
  • Generated blocks and files (ADR index, specs index, open-question counts, docs/architecture/dependencies.md) are rebuilt with make docs-generate and make deps-report; CI fails when they are stale.
  • Preview the site with make docs (http://127.0.0.1:8001); make docs-build builds it with --strict. Navigation is in mkdocs.yml; never move a file only for the site.
  • Releases: docs/releasing.md.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Fill in every section of the PR template, including the acceptance-criteria checklist, the dependency/licence table and the data/privacy checklist.
  • New dependencies must have an AGPL-compatible licence (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0, LGPL, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0). The licenses CI check fails otherwise. State each new dependency's licence in the PR.
  • CI runs only the workflows affected by your change (core, backend, frontend, containers, licenses, plus dco).
  • When an agent opens a PR at a maintainer's request, it assigns that maintainer (gh pr create --assignee <login>, or @me when gh runs as their account; step 5 of "Workflow for tickets" in AGENTS.md). Why: the PR then appears in their assigned list, ready for review and UAT. A bot account must name the maintainer's login, not @me.

docs.title: Changing the rules
docs.text:
Rules live only in AGENTS.md files (root and area folders). To add, change or remove one:

  1. Open an issue or a PR on a branch docs/rule-<short-name>, titled docs(rules): <summary>, and list each rule added, changed or removed.
  2. Put the rule in the right file: the root AGENTS.md if it applies everywhere, otherwise the area AGENTS.md, in short imperative wording. Add the same rule with a one-line reason (and an example if useful) to docs/conventions/<area>.md.
  3. If the rule can be enforced automatically (lint, type check, formatter, test, CI check), add that check instead or as well.
  4. Point out any conflict or overlap with existing rules in the PR instead of silently overriding them. Rules that change the method or a technical choice need an ADR or a decision in docs/specs/open-questions.md first.

The full procedure is in "Maintaining these instructions" in AGENTS.md. Claude Code users can run /add-rule <area>: <rule>, which follows it and asks for confirmation before editing.

docs.title: Proposing a method
docs.text:
Scientific methods (formulas, CPTs, thresholds, inference schemes) are specification first, code second:

  1. Open a Research question issue (template provided) citing the paper section and the relevant OQ-n, if any.
  2. Describe the options, their consequences, and references (verify every reference).
  3. Once agreed, the decision is recorded in docs/specs/open-questions.md (status decided, with reasoning and rejected options), the paper changes in docs/specs/paper-revisions.md, and the model in docs/specs/00-domain-model.md. Technical choices go into an ADR under docs/adr/.
  4. Only then is an implementation ticket opened, referencing the decision.

docs.title: How open questions are handled
docs.text:
• Open questions are listed in docs/specs/open-questions.md as OQ-n with status open, partly decided or decided.
  • Code never resolves an open question. Where code touches one, it references OQ-n in a docstring and leaves the behaviour undefined (abstract interface or NotImplementedError).
  • Tickets that depend on an open question carry the needs-spec label and wait for the decision.
  • If you need a modelling decision to proceed, write an ADR stub (status Proposed) or a research question; do not encode the choice silently.

docs.title: Data and privacy
docs.text:
• Never commit real personal or operational data. Synthetic data only, under core/tests/fixtures/ and data/synthetic/.
  • Request tickets are anonymous by design: spatial unit of origin, social group, service, facility (OQ-29) and timestamps only (see OQ-21).
  • No secrets in the repository. Use .env (gitignored) and keep .env.example current.
  • Attribute third-party data and record it in docs/data-sources.md.
  • Real open data (OpenStreetMap, ELSTAT, DEM, GTFS) is downloaded to data/local/ (git-ignored) by scripts, never committed.
  • Every processed dataset has a processing note DP-NNN in docs/data-processing/, copied from its TEMPLATE.md. Reusable QGIS models, scripts and projects go in data-processing/qgis/; QGIS is never a runtime dependency.
  • The synthetic demo dataset (data/synthetic/demo/, DP-001) is generated by scripts/generate_demo_data.py; regenerate it rather than editing files by hand.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: By contributing you agree that your contributions are licensed under the AGPL-3.0. The project name is covered by TRADEMARK.md, not by the licence.

docs.title: AGENTS.md
docs.text: Instructions for every coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) and every human contributor working in this repository. Area folders (core/, backend/, frontend/, data-processing/) have their own AGENTS.md with additional rules; read the one for the folder you work in. Human-readable explanations are in docs/conventions/.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
SolidarityNode is an open-source spatial probabilistic framework for estimating accessibility, latent social need, social vulnerability and resilience of social service networks (healthcare, social care and other public services). It uses Bayesian Networks (BN), Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBN) and spatial/network analysis. It is research software in early development.

Source of truth for the science: docs/specs/ (research description and per-module specs). If code and spec disagree, stop and flag it; do not silently pick one.

docs.title: Domain invariants (never violate)
docs.text:
1. Unit of analysis is spatial unit × social group × service × time. Core data structures and outputs are indexed by these four dimensions.
  2. Vulnerability is not resilience, and not risk. Vulnerability is the relationship that turns a disruption (group exposure, service loss) into consequences for a group given its social susceptibility; in code it is the CPT P(V | GE, SL, SS), evaluated at scenarios (Paper 3) or at observed disruptions (Paper 4), and learned from data as parameters (OQ-16). Resilience = dynamic property derived from the loss-and-recovery trajectory. Risk = vulnerability weighted by disruption probabilities. Separate modules, separate outputs. Never define resilience as just the inverse of recovery time, and never let vulnerability results depend on which scenarios a run includes.
  3. Facility state is not population service loss. A degraded facility does not imply lost coverage for a spatial unit if alternatives exist. Coverage is computed at the network level.
  4. Observed demand is not need. Latent need is estimated explicitly; keep observed demand and estimated need as distinct quantities. Hidden need (never expressed), unmet expressed need (requests not fulfilled) and met need never overlap; take-up means expressing need, not being served (OQ-8).
  5. Social group is not social susceptibility. The group says who is being examined; susceptibility is the probability that the group faces increased difficulty under given conditions.
  6. Outputs carry uncertainty. Prefer distributions or intervals to point estimates. Never collapse uncertainty silently.
  7. Operational support is a system response, not an independent resilience measure.
  8. Digital Twin is a future direction, not an assumption. Do not build twin-specific machinery yet.
  9. Keep variable kinds distinct. BN nodes, computed simulation variables and scenario parameters are different things (see docs/specs/00-domain-model.md, section 4). Do not turn one into another without an ADR.
  10. Decisions feed the papers. When a ticket or ADR changes the method, update docs/specs/paper-revisions.md (what changes in which paper section, and why) in the same PR.
  11. Open questions are not yours to resolve. docs/specs/open-questions.md lists what the papers leave unspecified. Implement only what a spec states; reference OQ-n in code and tickets; if a ticket needs an unresolved answer, stop and comment on the issue.

docs.title: Architecture rules
docs.text:
• Monorepo: core/ (Python library), backend/ (API), frontend/ (web UI), docs/, .github/.
  • Dependency direction: backend → core. core MUST NOT import from backend or frontend, and MUST NOT depend on web frameworks or a database driver.
  • core modules (map in docs/specs/00-domain-model.md): model, bayes, accessibility, demand, capacity, service_gap, latent_need, scenarios, vulnerability, operations, dynamics, resilience, uncertainty, sensitivity, validation. Each exposes a small typed public API; internals are private.
  • Long-running simulations run as background jobs, never inside a request handler.
  • Large datasets live in files (Parquet), metadata and results indexes in PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
  • Significant decisions are recorded as short ADRs in docs/adr/.

docs.title: Stack (initial choices; change via ADR)
docs.text:
• Python 3.12, uv for environments, ruff (lint + format), mypy (strict in core), pytest.
  • Backend: FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL with PostGIS.
  • Core: NumPy, pandas, GeoPandas, NetworkX/OSMnx for network analysis, pgmpy (BN/DBN; evaluate limits via ADR before committing).
  • Frontend: React + TypeScript (strict), Vite, pnpm, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier, Playwright (end-to-end). Map library: Leaflet (ADR 0007).
  • Docs: MkDocs with the Material theme, versioned with mike, published to GitHub Pages (ADR 0018); tooling locked in tools/docs/.
  • Containers: Podman (rootless) is the default engine; Docker must keep working. The engine and compose command are set once in the Makefile (CONTAINER_ENGINE ?= podman, COMPOSE ?= podman compose) and are overridable from the environment. Never hard-code docker in scripts, docs or CI; call the Makefile variables instead. Compose files follow the Compose spec (compose.yaml) and images use fully qualified names (for example docker.io/postgis/postgis:...), since Podman requires them. Avoid privileged ports (<1024) and rootful-only features. Everything runs locally with make up.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Requires uv, Node.js 26 with pnpm 12, and Podman (or Docker). make help lists all targets.

  • make setup — check that uv, node and pnpm are on PATH (names any missing), create .env from .env.example if missing (warns about missing keys), then install locked dependencies (uv sync --locked in core/ and backend/, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in frontend/)
  • make lint — ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy (strict) for core and backend; eslint, prettier --check and tsc for frontend; the platform version and the generated docs blocks are current
  • make test — fast, no container engine: unit and integration tests only, pytest (core; backend on a throw-away database on an existing PostGIS server: the db service of make up or make test-db, or SOLIDARITYNODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL) and Vitest (frontend)
  • make test-e2e — the Playwright end-to-end test, also run in CI: a separate throw-away stack (compose project solidaritynode-e2e on ports 18080/18000/15432, seeded with demo package 1.0.0 and removed afterwards); Playwright runs in its official image, E2E_LOCAL=1 uses a host browser
  • make fmt — ruff fix/format, prettier, eslint --fix
  • make up / make down — start/stop db, backend, worker and frontend with $(COMPOSE) (default podman compose); frontend http://127.0.0.1:8080, backend http://127.0.0.1:8000; passes GIT_COMMIT to the image builds
  • make logs, make ps, make wait, make stop SERVICE=… — follow logs, show containers, wait until the backend is ready, stop one service (for example worker)
  • make db-shell — psql in the database container with the credentials from .env
  • make seed — import demo package 1.0.0 (no-op if present), create the demo users when APP_ENV=development, wait for queued runs
  • make import-package PKG=<dir or archive> — validate, preview and (after typing yes, or YES=1) import a data package
  • make activate-version VERSION=<x.y.z> — make an earlier imported data version active again (rollback; queues a baseline run, revalidates scenarios; asks for yes unless YES=1)
  • make create-admin — create the first administrator interactively
  • make schemas — export docs/schemas/scenario.schema.json and openapi.json, regenerate the frontend API types
  • make reset — delete the database and results volumes, start, migrate and seed; asks for yes unless FORCE=1
  • make uat — reset then up, then print the URLs and demo credentials (UAT: docs/uat/)
  • make env — create .env if missing and warn about missing keys
  • make check-config APP_ENV=production — validate backend settings in a one-off container (refuses change-me secrets outside development and test)
  • make images — build images with $(CONTAINER_ENGINE)
  • make licenses — fail on dependency licences incompatible with AGPL-3.0
  • make docs / make docs-build — serve the documentation site on http://127.0.0.1:8001 / build it with --strict (CI); make docs-links checks links with lychee
  • make docs-generate — regenerate the ADR index, the specs index and the open-question counts (never edit those blocks by hand)
  • make deps-report — regenerate docs/architecture/dependencies.md from the lock files (after make setup); CI fails if it is stale or a licence is not allowed
  • make version / make version-sync — print the platform version / write VERSION into the manifests and locks (VERSION is the only place to change it; docs/releasing.md)
  • make labels — create GitHub labels from .github/labels.yml (needs gh auth login)
  • make clean / make distclean — remove caches and build output / also virtualenvs and node_modules
  • Per component: make lint-core, test-core, lint-backend, test-backend, lint-frontend, test-frontend
  • Docker instead of Podman: CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker COMPOSE="docker compose" make up
  • Regenerate the synthetic demo dataset: python3 scripts/generate_demo_data.py (update DP-001); rebuild the demo packages: python3 scripts/build_demo_packages.py (update DP-002)

Run make lint test before every commit. Do not mark work done if either fails.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Type hints everywhere in Python; no untyped public functions.
  • Small, pure, testable functions in core. Randomness goes through an explicit seed/numpy.random.Generator argument.
  • Every public function in core has a docstring stating its inputs, outputs, units and the spec section it implements (for example Spec §3.1).
  • Tests live next to the code's package in tests/. Use synthetic fixtures only.
  • Commits: Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, test:, refactor:, chore:), signed off with git commit -s (DCO).
  • Branches: feat/<issue-number>-short-name. One ticket, one branch, one PR. Reference the issue in the PR (Closes #N).

docs.title: Documentation rules
docs.text:
• Diagrams in docs are Mermaid code blocks in the Markdown files (flowcharts for structure and data flow, sequence diagrams for lifecycles, state diagrams for statuses, entity-relationship diagrams for data models). No image files and no other diagram tools for diagrams. Update a diagram in the same PR as the change it describes.
  • Every PR that changes behaviour adds a line under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md and updates the user guide page it affects (docs/user-guide/).
  • Do not copy what lives elsewhere; link to the single source: issues and plans in GitHub (project Kintsugi, milestones), open questions in docs/specs/open-questions.md, decisions in docs/adr/, method in docs/specs/.
  • Generated content (ADR index, specs index, open-question counts, docs/architecture/dependencies.md) comes from scripts and is checked in CI; never edit it by hand.
  • Do not move a file under docs/ that code, tests or AGENTS.md link to; change the site navigation in mkdocs.yml instead.

docs.title: Data and privacy rules
docs.text:
• Never commit real personal or operational data. Only synthetic data under core/tests/fixtures/ and data/synthetic/.
  • The request-logging mechanism must be anonymous by design: store only spatial unit of origin, social group, service type, the facility where the request is made or scheduled (OQ-29) and timestamps. No names, contact details, exact addresses or device identifiers. The facility raises re-identification risk in small units and follows the OQ-21 rules (minimum cell sizes, aggregation, retention); no ticket is stored until they are decided (ADR 0010).
  • No secrets in the repo. Use .env (gitignored) and keep .env.example current.
  • Configuration: the platform must run in development with no manual editing of .env. make setup creates .env from .env.example if missing and warns about keys present in .env.example but missing from .env. Every new setting is added to .env.example in the same PR, with a safe development default (secrets as change-me), a one-line comment, and an entry in the configuration section of CONTRIBUTING.md. Production values are never committed.
  • Third-party data (for example OpenStreetMap) must be attributed and its license respected; record sources in docs/data-sources.md.
  • Every processed dataset has a processing note in docs/data-processing/ (DP-NNN, from TEMPLATE.md), with exact steps, versions and checks. Reusable processing lives in data-processing/qgis/ (Processing models, scripts, projects with relative paths). When code or a ticket changes how data are prepared, update or add the note in the same PR. QGIS is a tool for preparing data, never a runtime dependency of core or backend.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text: • Project license: AGPL-3.0. New dependencies must have AGPL-compatible licenses (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0 are fine; no GPL-incompatible or proprietary-only dependencies). State the license of any new dependency in the PR description.

docs.title: Workflow for tickets
docs.text:
1. Read the issue fully, including acceptance criteria and the linked spec section.
  2. If anything is ambiguous or the spec is silent, do not invent methodology: comment on the issue with the question and stop.
  3. Plan briefly, implement in small commits, add tests that cover each acceptance criterion.
  4. Update docs and the spec cross-reference if behaviour changed: the user guide page, a line under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md, and Mermaid diagrams.
  5. Run make lint test (and make docs-build when docs changed), then open a PR using the template, assigned to the maintainer who asked for it (gh pr create --assignee <their-login>; see "Pull requests" in CONTRIBUTING.md). Do not merge your own PR.

Every paper issue carries both the paper:N label and the Kintsugi Paper field with the same value (the label makes issue search links work; the field drives the project views), plus the paper's milestone (v0.3 Paper 1 Accessibility … v0.6 Paper 4 Resilience).

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
• All acceptance criteria met and covered by tests.
  • Lint, type check and tests pass locally and in CI.
  • Public API documented; relevant docs/ updated, including the user guide page and a CHANGELOG.md line under Unreleased when behaviour changed.
  • No real data, no secrets, no new dependency without a license check.
  • Domain invariants above still hold.

docs.title: Maintaining these instructions
docs.text:
• Rules live in AGENTS.md files only. CLAUDE.md files are bridges (they import AGENTS.md) and never contain project rules. Do not create AGENT.md (singular) or other copies of the rules.
  • When asked to add, change or remove a rule:
  • Decide the area: root (applies everywhere), frontend, backend, core or data-processing.
  • If the rule can be enforced automatically (lint, type check, formatter, test, CI check), implement that instead or as well, and say so.
  • Check for conflicts or duplicates with existing rules in the root and area files; report them instead of silently overriding.
  • Edit the area AGENTS.md (short, imperative wording) and the matching docs/conventions/<area>.md (rule plus one-line reason and, if useful, an example). Root rules live in this file.
  • Do it on a branch docs/rule-<short-name> and open a PR titled docs(rules): <summary>, listing each rule added, changed or removed.
  • If a new area is needed (for example docs/ or .github/), create <folder>/AGENTS.md, its bridge <folder>/CLAUDE.md (containing only @AGENTS.md) and docs/conventions/<folder>.md in the same way.
  • Keep each area file short (under about 60 lines); move explanations to docs/conventions/.
